overview: Liverpool began as league champions and added the Charity Shield with a 1–0 win over Everton at Goodison Park. Roger Hunt supplied the goal. Most of the side that had delivered the 1966 title remained in place, with Ron Yeats, Tommy Smith and Tommy Lawrence at its centre and Ian Callaghan and Peter Thompson regulars on the wings.

The defence of the championship lasted well into the spring. Liverpool were still top after beating Stoke City on 4 March, but won only two of their final eleven league matches and finished fifth, nine points behind Manchester United. Hunt remained the leading scorer with 19 goals across all competitive matches, including the Shield. Liverpool scored 64 league goals in total.

Europe brought a much harsher assessment. Liverpool needed a third match in Brussels to overcome Petrolul Ploiești in the opening round of the European Cup. Ajax then won the first leg in Amsterdam 5–1; a 2–2 draw at Anfield left Liverpool out by 7–3 on aggregate. The FA Cup ended with another visit to Goodison Park, where Everton won the fifth-round tie 1–0 in March.

Bill Shankly had begun to add younger players without yet dismantling his established team. Emlyn Hughes arrived from Blackpool for £65,000 in February and made his debut in the March win over Stoke. Peter Wall, signed from Wrexham in October, was still waiting for his chance, while Dave Wilson’s move from Preston produced only one first-team appearance. Gordon Milne left for Blackpool in May. The season therefore combined a fading title challenge with the first changes to the group that had brought Liverpool back to the top.

events.title: The Charity Shield stays on Merseyside
events.detail: Hunt scored the only goal as Liverpool beat FA Cup holders Everton at Goodison Park.

events.title: A third match settles the European tie
events.detail: Liverpool beat Petrolul Ploiești 2–0 in Brussels after the two legs had finished 3–3 on aggregate.

events.title: Ajax end the European Cup campaign
events.detail: A 5–1 defeat in Amsterdam was followed by a 2–2 draw at Anfield. Hunt scored both Liverpool goals in the return, but Ajax advanced 7–3 on aggregate.

events.title: Hughes makes his Liverpool debut
events.detail: The February signing from Blackpool appeared in the 2–1 league win over Stoke City at Anfield.

events.title: Everton win the FA Cup derby
events.detail: Liverpool’s FA Cup run ended in the fifth round with a 1–0 defeat at Goodison Park.

researchNotes: Competitive goal totals include the Charity Shield: Hunt’s 19 comprises 14 league goals, one FA Cup goal, three European Cup goals and one Shield goal. Both LFChistory and 11v11 give 19.

Summer moves are assigned to the season they immediately precede. Ray Clemence’s June 1967 arrival therefore appears in 1967–68, although LFChistory groups it under 1966–67. Milne’s departure is dated on the final matchday, 13 May 1967, and remains here.

The official Dave Wilson profile places his only appearance away at Blackpool; the match record and LFChistory profile establish Anfield, 13 May 1967. The home venue is used. Wall’s fee is omitted because the transfer listing flags a linked deal with Stuart Mason.
Key players were selected from their involvement this season. Hughes is recorded as an important arrival and event, rather than being selected solely for his later Liverpool career.
